llm.summary: This small skill only guides an agent to search GitHub for code examples, with no executable code, persistence, credential use, or destructive behavior found.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is GitHub code and implementation discovery, and the runtime workflow is limited to building search queries, using WebSearch or optionally GitHub API search, parsing results, ranking them, and returning findings.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The triggers include broad single words such as "code" and "search", which could cause accidental invocation outside clearly GitHub-specific requests, but the body also states when to use and not use the skill.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains only a markdown SKILL.md file; no install scripts, binaries, hooks, or executable components were present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Network search behavior is proportionate to a GitHub code-search skill, and there is no evidence of local codebase scanning, broad private data indexing, mutation, or credential/session access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No persistence, background workers, privilege escalation, local auth store access, or automatic long-running behavior appears in the artifacts.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install this if you want GitHub implementation searches, but be aware it may activate on generic "code" or "search" requests; review generated searches if you want to avoid unnecessary external web queries.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad trigger set is artifact-backed and not ideal for a GitHub-specific search skill, but it affects routing reliability rather than granting high-impact authority or showing hidden behavior.
[TR1] unexpected: The bare "code" trigger is overbroad for this purpose, but the skill text does not instruct credential use, local data access, mutation, or automatic execution.
[TR2] unexpected: The bare "search" trigger could conflict with built-in search behavior, but the resulting action is disclosed GitHub/WebSearch research and remains proportionate.
